title: How to Calculate Your Real Estate Agent Salary: Hourly to Annual Guide
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay for a real estate agent salary. Use our 38-hour week formula, see tax and super estimates, and understand award rates.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 gross per year. You can use [the timesheet](/) to do this calculation automatically, including casual loading if applicable.

faqs.q: What is the average real estate agent salary?
faqs.a: According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026, full-time ordinary time earnings in the rental, hiring and real estate industry average $1979.60 per week. This is an industry average, not a job median. Based on a 38-hour week, that equates to an annual gross salary of approximately $102,939 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary by your employer. For example, on a $60,000 annual salary, super would be $7,200 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

If you earn an hourly wage or receive a salary offer, converting between the two helps you compare jobs and plan your finances. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks in a year. For most full-time employees, a 38-hour week is the benchmark under the Fair Work Act. This guide explains the conversion, how tax and super affect your take-home pay, and what the industry average for a real estate agent salary looks like.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. If you work 38 hours per week, the calculation becomes:

- $26.44 per hour (National Minimum Wage) × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 per year
- $33.05 per hour (casual rate including 25% loading) × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80 per year

You can use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top – never type a rate that already includes casual loading. The timesheet also shows your fortnightly pay (weekly × 2) and annual figures.

### Real Estate Agent Salary: An Industry Average

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that full-time ordinary time weekly earnings in the rental, hiring and real estate industry averaged $1979.60 per week in May 2026. This is an industry average, not a job median. To find the implied hourly rate, divide by 38 hours: $1979.60 ÷ 38 ≈ $52.09 per hour. The annual gross equivalent is $1979.60 × 52 = $102,939.20. Remember, this figure excludes super, tax, and any overtime or allowances.

When you read about a real estate agent salary, it’s important to check whether the figure is a median for the occupation or an industry average. The ABS data covers all roles in the sector, including administrative staff, property managers, and sales agents. For a more precise estimate of your own pay, use your actual hourly rate or salary offer.

### Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. Many industries have award rates that are higher than the minimum. For example, the Real Estate Industry Award sets minimum pay rates for different classifications. Always check the relevant award via [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

Casual loading compensates for the lack of paid leave. If you are casual, your employer must pay the loading on top of your base rate. Do not include the loading when entering your rate into [the timesheet](/) – use the checkbox instead.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To estimate your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a real estate agent earning the industry average weekly of $1979.60, the fortnightly gross is $3959.20. This can help you align your budget with your pay cycle. The timesheet shows both weekly and fortnightly figures automatically.

### Tax on Your Annual Salary

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a gross annual salary of $102,939 (industry average real estate agent salary), the estimated tax would be approximately $24,267 plus Medicare of $2,059, leaving about $76,613 after tax. This is an estimate only – your actual tax depends on your circumstances, including any deductions or offsets.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It does not reduce your take-home pay. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830. For a $102,939 salary, super would be $12,353 per year. If you earn above the base, super only applies to the first $270,830. You can read more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) to understand salary sacrifice options.

### Using the Timesheet for Your Own Calculations

[The timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your hourly rate and see annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. It applies the standard 38-hour week but you can adjust hours if you work a different pattern. The tool also estimates tax and super based on the current rates. Remember the disclaimer: annual pay here is hourly × hours per week × 52, assuming the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed reference tables, visit [reference tables](/data) to compare award rates and industry averages. If you want to check the current minimum wage, see [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage). For take-home pay after tax and super, the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides further guidance.
